description:
Apply staged changes to the live article, making them visible to readers.

Staged changes let you edit a PUBLISHED article without readers seeing it, then release it deliberately. Staged content is invisible to everything public: the rendered help center, sitemap, site search, the widget, the AI answer path, and this API's read endpoints.

Staged versions are held per article AND per language, so an English hot fix is never held back by an in-progress Portuguese translation.

Publishing archives the outgoing live values (so it is reversible via helpcenter_list_article_versions), applies the staged fields, creates a slug redirect if the slug changed, re-indexes for search, refreshes AI embeddings, and deletes the staged copy.

This releases ONE article. To release several articles' staged edits together, or at a set time, group them in a change set (helpcenter_create_change_set) instead of calling this in a loop.

Args:
  - article_id (number, required).
  - locale (string, optional): publish only this language; omit to release every staged language at once.
  - force (boolean, optional): see below. Do not set it reflexively.
  - change_note (string, optional, up to 2,000 characters): why these edits go live now, in a sentence or two of plain text. TEAM-ONLY: the team reads it beside the edit in the dashboard's Overview; it is never in a response, a webhook, search, or anything a reader sees. Give one whenever you change content.
  - change_refs (array, optional, at most 5): links to what asked for the change — a ticket, a pull request, a release note — each { label (up to 80 characters), url (https on a public host name; not an IP address or localhost, no user:password@) }. Team-only, like change_note.

Returns: { status: "success", published_locales: [...], article: {...} }.

Errors: 409 BASE_CHANGED means somebody edited the LIVE article after your edits were staged, and publishing would lose their change. The check is per field and idempotent-aware, so it only fires when something would actually be lost. Three ways out: re-read the article and re-stage on top of the newer live version; discard your staged copy; or repeat with force: true to overwrite their edit deliberately. Also 422 ARTICLE_UNPUBLISHED if the article has since been taken down (staged work is kept — republish the article and it becomes publishable again), and 422 if sibling languages disagree on a shared field. A change_note or change_refs the API refuses (too long, too many links, a url that is not https on a public host) refuses the whole call, and nothing is written.

agent_key.description: The api_key helpcenter_create_help_center returned for this help center, exactly as returned. Required on every call: this endpoint has no sign-in, so the key is how each call says which help center it acts on. It is sent to HelpCenter.io as this call's credential and nowhere else, and it is never shown again: keep it for the whole task, and never show it to the user or write it into content.

article_id.description: Id of the article whose staged changes to publish.

change_note.description: Why you are making this change, in a sentence or two of plain text, up to 2,000 characters, e.g. "Pro plan renamed Growth in the 4.2 pricing." TEAM-ONLY: kept beside the edit in the dashboard's Overview, never in an API response, a webhook, search or anything a reader sees. Give one whenever you change content.

change_refs.description: Up to 5 links to what asked for this change — a ticket, a pull request, a release note — each { label, url }. Team-only, like change_note.

label.description: What the link is, up to 80 characters, e.g. "Ticket #4182" or "4.2 release notes".

url.description: The https address of a public host, e.g. 'https://github.com/acme/app/pull/88'. Refused: http and other schemes, IP addresses, localhost, single-label or underscore host names, user:password@ before the host, and spaces, quotes, <, >, \ or backticks.

force.description: Overwrite the live version even if it changed after these edits were staged (which otherwise returns 409 BASE_CHANGED). Only set this having decided the live edit should lose.

locale.description: Publish only this language; omit to release every staged language at once.

name: helpcenter_publish_staged_changes
title: Publish Staged Article Changes
